title: A new approach to measure interocular suppression in amblyopia and strabismus
author: Hou

steps.title: Set up display hardware
steps.instruction: Place two identical Sony CRT monitors at a viewing distance of 86 cm from the participant, connect them for dichoptic presentation, and arrange a mirror stereoscope so that each eye views one monitor; adjust the mirrors so the nonius lines can be aligned under the participant's best optical correction.

steps.title: Configure stimulus parameters
steps.instruction: Program the visual stimuli as a vertical bar in one eye and a horizontal bar in the other eye, each with spatial frequency 1 cpd and contrast 35 %; set stimulus duration to 60–100 ms (use 100 ms for the protocol) and follow each stimulus with a 200 ms noise mask; ensure the bars are highly visible to the amblyopic eye.

steps.title: Calibrate bar length for monocular visibility
steps.instruction: Present the bars monocularly to the amblyopic (or non‑fixating) eye and iteratively adjust the bar length until the observer correctly identifies the bar orientation on at least 75 % of trials; record this calibrated length for use in subsequent mixed binocular/monocular trials.

steps.title: Create trial block structure
steps.instruction: Generate a block of trials (e.g., 100 trials) in which 50 trials are binocular presentations (one eye receives the vertical bar, the other the horizontal bar, with the horizontal bar randomly assigned to either eye) and 50 trials are monocular presentations (a single bar shown to either the left or right eye with equal probability—25 left‑eye trials and 25 right‑eye trials); randomize the order of all trials.

steps.title: Run experimental trials
steps.instruction: For each trial, display a central fixation point and the nonius lines to verify stereoscope alignment, have the participant self‑initiate the trial, present the stimulus for 100 ms, immediately present a 200 ms noise mask, then collect the participant’s response without time limit or feedback; the participant reports whether they saw one or two bars and indicates the orientation(s) by pressing the horizontal‑arrow button for a horizontal bar and the vertical‑arrow button for a vertical bar.

steps.title: Compute suppression metric
steps.instruction: Calculate the percent of correct orientation responses for monocular trials and for binocular trials for the amblyopic (or non‑fixating) eye; compute the depth of suppression as the ratio binocular % / monocular % (values < 1 indicate stronger suppression).
